text:
alex.w: quick idea — can we slim the public rate-limit surface? current RPM + TPM + concurrency + burst options is confusing for customers and our console. propose: canonical controls = RPM (requests/min) and concurrency cap; keep burst credits as an opt-in additive. TPM (token-per-min) should be a derived, model-aware view. thoughts? :thinking:

marta: strong +1 for simplifying. customers ask "what is my limit" and we show 4 numbers today lol. RPM+concurrency is easier to explain on invoices/console.

devon: caution — a lot of users care about token limits because of chatty completions. deriving TPM means we need reliable model tokenization estimates per model and version. that data lives in model-profiles but coverage is incomplete.

samir: can we make TPM a computed metric in UI only, not an enforcement primitive? enforcement stays on RPM/concurrency and bursts. then we show "estimated tokens/min" next to the RPM.

june: UX note — console should show the effective limit per-route and effective fallback policy. when a tenant hits concurrency cap we currently return 429 with generic text. we should provide a header with diagnostic fields: `X-Rate-Limit-Reason` + `X-Org-Limit-Id` so they can trace.

alex.w: agreed on headers. also want a migration plan: deploy enforcement in soft-mode (log+metrics) for 2 weeks, expose graphs in infra dashboards and in the console tenant page, then flip to hard-enforce. ops will need a way to grant temporary burst credits for support cases.

marta: +1 to soft-mode. for burst credits I'm thinking of a decaying bucket that refills at a per-minute rate but also stores short-term extra credits consumed from a 1h burst pool. that matches how we throttle today.

devon: rough config sketch (for discussion):
```json
{
  "org_id": "org_123",
  "limits": {
    "rpm": 1200,
    "concurrency": 40,
    "burst_pool": {
      "capacity": 600,
      "window_secs": 3600
    }
  },
  "enforcement_mode": "soft" // soft | hard
}
```

samir: implementation notes: runtime already supports token-level accounting for batching; hooking RPM enforcement is straightforward at the edge router. concurrency needs cross-host counters (we have that via our lease service), burst pool can be implemented as a distributed leaky-bucket per-org. we should expose both `tokens_used` and `requests_used` metrics for SLO debugging.

june: console needs two things: (1) a single "effective limit" card that explains how RPM & concurrency interplay with bursts (text + example), (2) a timeline showing soft-mode violations and support-granted pockets. customers love concrete examples like "if you hit concurrency=40, a 10-request parallel fanout of 10k tokens will be rate-limited even if RPM not exceeded".

alex.w: ops-bot — can you create an infra ticket for the soft-mode rollout and add a dashboard with these panels: rpm/reqs_per_min, concurrency_in_use, burst_pool_level, soft-mode_violations?

ops-bot: created ticket INFRA-4721: "soft-mode per-org limits rollout". Deploy note: rate-service v2 can be rolled with soft enforcement flag. :white_check_mark:

marta: what about per-key vs per-org ambiguity? some customers use multiple API keys per org for product isolation. enforcement at per-org level will aggregate across keys; we should surface per-key breakdown for billing and debugging but keep enforcement aggregated.

devon: agree. also raise: chained fallbacks — if org hits limit, route requests to a lower-cost model variant automatically (if tenant opted in). that preserves availability for degradable workloads. needs routing-policy and telemetry hooks.

samir: telemetry: add labels `org.id`, `key.id`, `route`, `model.variant`, `enforcement_mode`, `violation_type` to all rate metrics. create an alert when soft-mode violation rate > 1% of traffic for 10m.

alex.w: action items:
- devon/marta: finalize policy proto and edge hook changes (this week)
- samir: design distributed burst-pool implementation + metrics (by Tue)
- june: console copy & panels + per-key breakdown (mock by Thu)
- ops: run soft-mode for infra tenants first, roll progressively (INFRA-4721)

june: also propose showing the single "effective limit" in the onboarding flow so customers don't get stuck picking weird combos.

alex.w: love that. +1. we'll run RFC with security and billing before hard-enforce. thanks all :thumbsup:
